"Empirical Multi-Objective Optimization, Mininet Emulation & AI Complexity Tax Auditing"

1 Background, Problem & 3-Axis Formulation

CPP Formulation

Software Defined Networking (SDN) decouples control intelligence from packet-forwarding hardware [1]–[3]. Across multi-site Wide Area Networks (WANs), partitioning switches across k controllers among N sites is the NP-hard Controller Placement Problem (CPP) [4], [6], [7].

The Methodological Gap & Complexity Tax (ω): Recent Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) studies (MuZero [12], CAPFUL [14], AP-DQN [15]) evaluate neural policies against trivial baselines on single-metric latency, omitting offline training overhead (ωtrain vs. online inference τinf), graph structure sensitivity, and Open vSwitch kernel delays [6], [9].
1. Mean Propagation Latency: L(C) = (1/|V|) Σv∈V minc∈C dG(v, c)  (1)
2. Single-Link (N−1) Reachability: Reachavg(C) = (1/|E|) Σe∈E (1/|V|) Σv∈V Ireach(v, G\{e}, C)  (2)
3. Ideal-Point Pareto Distance: Dideal(C) = √[0.5·L̂² + 0.3·(1 − R̂avg)² + 0.2·ω̂²]  (3)

2 Research Questions & Topology Corpus

N_obs = 300 Design
RQ1 (Latency & N−1 Survivability): Do PyTorch DQN [15] and Bandit RL achieve statistically significant reductions in L(C) and improvements in Reachavg(C) over Greedy K-Center [4], K-Means [8], and GA [10]?
RQ2 (Offline Training ωtrain vs. Online Inference τinf): How does computational overhead scale across N ∈ {20, 50}, k ∈ {2, 3, 5}, and after how many link-churn epochs (Tbreak) does DQN amortize ωtrain?
RQ3 (Topology Geometry & Mininet Validation): How do scale-free hub skew (BA) vs. spatial mesh structure (Waxman) and live OpenFlow kernel switching delays govern the 3D Pareto frontier?

3 5 Evaluated Placement Paradigms & Workflow

Methodology
1. Random Baseline O(k)
Controlled PRNG uniform sampling without replacement (lower bound).
2. Greedy K-Center [4],[7] O(k·N)
Farthest-first deterministic 2-approximation minimax radius traversal.
3. Spatial K-Means [8],[9] O(I·k·N)
Iterative shortest-path distance partitioning with discrete graph medoids.
4. Genetic Algorithm [10] O(G·P·kN)
Ppop=40, Gmax=50, tournament selection, uniform crossover, swap μ=0.15.
5. PyTorch Deep Q-Network (DQN) & Bandit RL [15] N→64→64→N MLP
ReLU MLP, Adam (α=0.001, γ=0.99), replay M=10,000, ε∈[1.0→0.05], Reward: R(C) = 10·(Lmax−L(C))/Lmax + 5·Reachavg(C).

4 Cross-Topology Factorial Benchmark (Table I) & 3D Pareto Frontier

ω_train vs. τ_inf
Fig. 2. 3-Axis Pareto space: Propagation Latency L(C) vs. N−1 Reachability Reach_avg(C) vs. Compute Tax ω(C).
1. GA Raw Latency Dominance: Across all 12 synthetic factorial cells, GA achieved lowest mean latency in 100% of cells (up to 55.29% below Random on Waxman N=20, k=5).
2. Topology & Menger's Theorem: 2-edge-connected graphs (Internet2, ATT-MPLS, BA m=2) guarantee 100.0% N−1 reachability; sparse Waxman graphs with bridge links drop to 94.5%–98.8% (96.1%–97.6% at k=3).
3. Training Tax vs. Forward Pass: Trained DQN inference is fast (τinf = 0.021–0.029 ms), but fixed-dimension MLPs require per-topology training (ωtrain = 58.3–21,260 ms).

Convergence & Post-Hoc Contrasts: DQN stabilizes at rolling mean reward 13.199 (grand mean 13.055 ± 0.589, peak 14.607, L(C) = 1.420 ms) but requires ωtrain = 21.26 s (11.40 s cached). Tukey HSD confirms GA & K-Means beat Random (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 1.42), while DQN vs. K-Means is statistically indistinguishable (t(8) = 0.42, p = 0.68).

Fig. 4. Bounded Deployment Flowchart (N ≤ 50).
1. Planar Mesh (N≤50) τ=3.2–5.3ms

Deploy Spatial K-Means: Zero training, best worst-case Mininet tail RTT (5.764 ms).

2. Scale-Free Core τ=0.03–0.21ms

Deploy Greedy K-Center: Captures BA hub nodes in sub-ms; 100% Pareto frontier.

3. Offline Planning τ=12.9–76.1ms

Deploy Genetic Alg. (GA): Lowest latency in 12/12 cells & best mean RTT (2.718 ms).

4. High-Churn WANs T* > 59–208 Ep

Deploy Pre-Trained DQN: Fast forward pass (0.021–0.026 ms/ep) amortizes ω_train.

8 Conclusions & Future Research Directions

Key Takeaways

• Static WAN Decision Efficiency (N ≤ 50): GA (2.718 ms RTT), K-Means (2.852 ms RTT), and Greedy K-Center (2.934 ms RTT) outperform DRL (3.056 ms RTT) without incurring the 21.26 s offline neural training tax.

• Dynamic Churn Amortization Boundary: Pre-trained PyTorch DQN inference (0.021–0.026 ms/epoch) amortizes ωtrain after T* = 59.0–65.2 epochs vs. GA and 145.8–207.6 epochs vs. K-Means, though classical heuristics retain lower post-churn latency.

• Future Directions: (1) Live Mininet NetFlow switch-migration traces; (2) Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for topology-agnostic zero-shot generalization (N ∈ [100, 500]); (3) Multi-link (N−k) failures & ONOS/Ryu Raft east-west synchronization.
